answers.value: The prospective MGA/coverholder under due diligence for a new binding authority: its audited financial statements (last 3 years), solvency/net-worth position, E&O and fidelity cover, and operational capacity to hold and account for the delegated line. Scope = one coverholder due-diligence file in the delegated-authority (DA) module.

The current onboarding assessment cycle: financials for the 3 most recent audited year-ends plus the trailing 12 months of management accounts; assessment completed within 15 business days of receiving a complete application pack.

Required fields on the DA due-diligence record: legal entity name, FEIN, audited net worth, current ratio, working capital, E&O limit/retention, and premium trust account confirmation. A financial-standing rating (Strong/Adequate/Weak) is assigned; any blank mandatory field returns the file to the coverholder for completion.

Net worth and premium-held figures on the assessment reconcile to the audited balance sheet and the latest bordereaux; premium trust balances tie to the billing/commission ledger within a 1% tolerance. Any variance above tolerance is documented before sign-off.

The completed financial-standing assessment (PDF) plus supporting statements are filed to GRC under /delegated-authority/<coverholder-id>/due-diligence/financial/ with immutable timestamp and version label v<n>; retained 7 years past authority termination per the DA record-retention schedule.

A "Weak" or below-threshold financial rating is logged as a due-diligence exception in GRC with disposition (decline / conditional approval with reduced limit / require parental guarantee), owner = Delegated Authority Manager, and a documented rationale before the file advances.

Assessment cites the internal Delegated Authority Underwriting Policy s.4 (coverholder financial-standing thresholds) and Lloyd’s/ Managing General Agent minimum-standards MS9 on delegated authority; premium trust handling cited against state fiduciary rules.
Retention requirement met: due-diligence file held 7 years beyond authority termination, matching the DA retention schedule; retention flag set on the GRC record at filing.

No external regulatory filing deadline; internal SLA is assessment complete before the binding-authority decision and no later than 15 business days after a complete pack. Deadline field tracks the DA committee date.
All new-coverholder financial-standing assessments completed in the period plus a 25% sample of annual re-assessments of existing coverholders (minimum 10 files).

PASS = net worth ≥ policy minimum for the requested limit, positive working capital, valid in-force E&O ≥ required limit, and confirmed segregated premium trust account. FAIL = any threshold breached without a documented, manager-approved mitigant.

Failed files are held (not bound), referred to the Delegated Authority Manager, and either declined or approved with conditions (limit cap, guarantee, shortened review cycle) recorded on the GRC exception; re-test on receipt of remediation evidence.
Effective dates = financial statement year-ends assessed through the assessment sign-off date; only figures dated within the trailing 36 months are treated as current.

Applicable rule: internal Delegated Authority Underwriting Policy s.4 coverholder financial-standing thresholds and premium-trust fiduciary requirements; no SERFF/DOI filing is generated by this internal assessment.

answers.value: The coverholder’s operational infrastructure for holding the delegated line: policy-issuance and rating systems, staffing and underwriter competency, compliance/complaints handling, bordereaux production capability, and IT/data security. Scope = one coverholder operational due-diligence assessment.

Current onboarding assessment cycle; systems and staffing reviewed as at the assessment date, with the prior 12 months of complaint and bordereaux-timeliness history examined. Completed within 15 business days of a complete pack.

Operational-capability record fields: PAS/rating platform in use, licensed underwriter headcount and authority levels, bordereaux format/frequency, complaints procedure, data-security attestation (SOC 2 / cyber cover). Each dimension scored 1–5; missing evidence blocks the score.

Declared policy/premium volumes and staffing ratios reconcile to the coverholder’s systems demo and sample bordereaux; declared in-force count ties to the test extract within tolerance before the capability score is finalised.

Operational assessment and evidence (system screenshots, org chart, SOC 2 report) filed to GRC under /delegated-authority/<coverholder-id>/due-diligence/operational/ with timestamp and version v<n>; retained 7 years past termination.

Any dimension scoring below the minimum (e.g. no documented complaints process, no data-security attestation) is logged as an exception in GRC with a remediation action and target date, owner = Delegated Authority Manager, before authority is granted.
Assessment uses the approved Coverholder Operational Capability scorecard v3.1 (weighted dimensions: systems, staffing, compliance, reporting, IT security); scorecard version recorded on the record.
Sensitivity: a one-band drop in the systems or reporting dimension is tested to confirm it does not change the overall onboard/decline recommendation; if it does, the file is referred up.
Materiality: any single dimension scoring 1 (critical gap) or an aggregate score below 3.0 is material and forces a referral regardless of the other dimensions.
Cited against the Delegated Authority Underwriting Policy s.5 (operational minimum standards) and Lloyd’s coverholder minimum standards MS9 (systems, controls and reporting).
Retention met: operational due-diligence file held 7 years beyond authority termination per the DA retention schedule; retention flag set at filing.
No external filing deadline; internal SLA is completion before the DA committee decision and within 15 business days of a complete pack.
All new-coverholder operational assessments in the period plus a 25% sample of annual re-assessments (minimum 10).
PASS = aggregate scorecard ≥ 3.0 with no dimension scoring 1 and a valid data-security attestation. FAIL = aggregate < 3.0, any dimension = 1, or missing security attestation.

FAIL files are held, referred to the Delegated Authority Manager, and either declined or approved with conditions (remediation plan, reduced scope, shortened audit cycle) recorded as a GRC exception; re-scored on remediation evidence.
Acceptance criteria: every operational dimension scored with evidence, aggregate ≥ 3.0, security attestation on file, and a documented onboard/decline recommendation.
Evidence in GRC /delegated-authority/<coverholder-id>/due-diligence/operational/, cross-linked to the coverholder record in the PAS DA module.
Approved methodology: Coverholder Operational Capability scorecard v3.1, weightings and thresholds owned by the Delegated Authority function; parameter source = DA governance library.

Field definitions from the DA data dictionary: systems_platform, licensed_headcount, bordereaux_frequency, complaints_flag, soc2_flag, dimension_scores[]; control total = declared in-force count vs test extract.
Applicable rule: Delegated Authority Underwriting Policy s.5 and Lloyd’s coverholder minimum standards MS9; no external regulatory filing produced.

answers.value: Approval of the renewed, modified, or terminated binding-authority (delegated underwriting) agreement with the coverholder: agreed classes, limits, territory, premium authority, commission, reporting obligations and duration. Scope = one binding-authority agreement.
Current renewal/amendment cycle; approval completed before the agreement effective/renewal date, typically finalised 30 days prior to expiry of the outgoing agreement.

Agreement record fields: coverholder id, classes, per-risk/aggregate limits, territory, premium authority, commission %, reporting/bordereaux obligations, effective and expiry dates, and approver. All terms must be populated and consistent with the latest audit/performance review before approval.

Approved limits and commission in the agreement reconcile to the authority matrix and the renewal recommendation; aggregate exposure implied by the limits reconciles to the portfolio plan. Variances resolved before sign.

The executed agreement and approval record are filed to GRC /delegated-authority/<coverholder-id>/agreement/ and attached to the PAS coverholder record with version and timestamp; retained 7 years past termination.

Adverse audit findings or performance deterioration are addressed as conditions on renewal (reduced limits, remediation milestones, non-renewal); each condition logged in GRC with owner = Delegated Authority Manager before approval.
Limit adequacy and pricing terms rest on the approved DA performance-analysis methodology v2.0 and the current portfolio plan; methodology version referenced on the approval.
Sensitivity: renewal terms stress-tested against an adverse loss-ratio scenario; if projected performance breaches appetite, limits/commission are tightened or the agreement is non-renewed.
Materiality: any change to classes, limits, territory or commission versus the expiring agreement is material and must be explicitly approved and documented.

Approval cites the Delegated Authority Underwriting Policy s.6 (agreement approval and renewal), the DA authority matrix v3.2, and Lloyd’s coverholder minimum standards MS9; surplus-lines terms cited where applicable.
Retention met: executed agreement and approval retained 7 years past termination per the DA retention schedule; retention flag set at filing.
No SERFF filing arises from the agreement itself; internal deadline is approval before the effective/renewal date, tracked against the expiry of the outgoing agreement.
All binding-authority agreements approved, renewed, amended or terminated in the period (census).

PASS = agreement terms within the authority matrix, consistent with the latest audit/performance review, and signed by an authorised approver before the effective date. FAIL = terms exceed matrix without escalation, conflict with review findings, or lack timely sign-off.
Out-of-matrix or adverse-finding cases are escalated to the Chief Underwriting Officer; the agreement is not activated in the PAS until an authorised approval with any conditions is recorded.
Acceptance criteria: complete agreed terms, reconciliation to the authority matrix and performance review, documented conditions, and authorised sign-off before the effective date.
Evidence in GRC /delegated-authority/<coverholder-id>/agreement/, linked to the executed contract and the PAS coverholder record.
Approved methodology: limit and pricing adequacy assessed via DA performance-analysis methodology v2.0 and the portfolio plan; parameter source = DA governance library and reserving guidance.
Applicable rule: Delegated Authority Underwriting Policy s.6, DA authority matrix v3.2, and Lloyd’s coverholder minimum standards MS9; surplus-lines eligibility cited for E&S classes.

answers.value: The coverholder audit record: audit findings, remediation evidence, and the authority renewal/non-renewal decision, archived for regulatory and Lloyd’s oversight access. Scope = one completed coverholder audit and renewal cycle.
Archived within 10 business days of the audit closing and the renewal decision being issued; retained for the full retention period thereafter.

Archive record fields: audit id, coverholder id, audit date, findings and ratings, remediation actions and closure evidence, renewal decision, and retention-until date. All findings must show a disposition and the renewal decision must be attached before the file is marked archived.
Count of archived findings reconciles to the audit report’s finding count, and each closed finding has linked remediation evidence; delta between report findings and archived findings must be 0.

Audit pack, remediation evidence and renewal decision archived to GRC /delegated-authority/<coverholder-id>/audit/<cycle>/ with immutable timestamp, version, and a retention-until date; write-once retention applied.
Open findings not yet remediated at archive are carried as tracked exceptions with owner (Delegated Authority Manager) and due dates; the archive flags them open so oversight can see status.
Retention/archival cited against the DA record-retention schedule, Lloyd’s coverholder oversight/audit access requirements, and the internal records-management policy.
Retention met: audit and renewal records retained 7 years past authority termination (or longer where a state DOI requires), with the retention-until date set and enforced on the GRC record.
No external filing deadline; internal SLA is archive complete within 10 business days of audit close and renewal decision. Deadline field tracks the archive-by date.
Every completed coverholder audit/renewal cycle in the period (census); each checked for a complete, retained archive.

PASS = findings, remediation evidence and renewal decision all archived with a retention-until date and accessible to oversight. FAIL = any missing component, no retention date, or an inaccessible/mutable archive.
Incomplete archives are returned to the analyst to attach the missing component before the cycle is closed; retention/access failures are escalated to the Records Manager.
Field definitions from the DA data dictionary: audit_id, coverholder_id, audit_date, finding_id, finding_rating, remediation_status, renewal_decision, retention_until.
Control total = archived finding count reconciles to the audit report finding count; each finding’s remediation-status field populated; 0 unmatched findings.
Applicable rule: DA record-retention schedule and Lloyd’s coverholder oversight/audit access requirements; internal records-management policy governs the write-once retention and access controls.
